title: Telescope homotopy colimits are termwise filtered colimits
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $E_0^\bullet\to E_1^\bullet\to\cdots$ be a sequence of cochain complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Define its homotopy colimit as the cone of $1-\operatorname{shift}:\bigoplus_n E_n^\bullet\to\bigoplus_n E_n^\bullet$. The canonical map from this homotopy colimit to the termwise filtered colimit $\varinjlim_n E_n^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules].

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Section 21.17, the telescope/colimit argument in Lemma 06YS

proof.text: Put $A^\bullet=\bigoplus_n E_n^\bullet$ and let $u=1-\operatorname{shift}:A^\bullet\to A^\bullet$. In each degree, an element of the direct sum has finite support; if $u(x)=0$, its first nonzero component cannot cancel with an earlier component, so the least component is zero, and induction gives $x=0$. Thus $u$ is termwise injective. The cokernel in degree $i$ is the quotient of $\bigoplus_n E_n^i$ by the relations identifying each element with its image in the next summand, which is exactly the filtered colimit $\varinjlim_n E_n^i$. These identifications commute with the differentials, so $\operatorname{coker}(u)$ is the termwise filtered-colimit complex.

With the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the cone of $u$ is $C(u)^r=A^r\oplus A^{r+1}$ with differential $(l,k)\mapsto(d(l)+u(k),-d(k))$. The map $\pi:C(u)\to\operatorname{coker}(u)$, $(l,k)\mapsto[l]$, is a termwise surjective chain map, since $[d(l)+u(k)]=[d(l)]$; this is the canonical map from $\operatorname{hocolim}_n E_n^\bullet=C(u)$ to $\varinjlim_n E_n^\bullet$ (Step 1). Its kernel $K^\bullet$ consists of the pairs $(u(c),k)$, with $c$ unique because $u$ is termwise injective (Step 1). $K^\bullet$ is contractible: $h(u(c),k)=(0,c)$, of degree $-1$, satisfies $dh+hd=1$, because $d(0,c)=(u(c),-d(c))$ and $h(d(u(c),k))=h(u(d(c)+k),-d(k))=(0,d(c)+k)$. Hence $H^i(K^\bullet)=0$ for all $i$. The degreewise short exact sequence $0\to K^\bullet\to C(u)\xrightarrow{\pi}\operatorname{coker}(u)\to0$ of complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules has the long exact cohomology sequence $\cdots\to H^i(K^\bullet)\to H^i(C(u))\xrightarrow{H^i(\pi)}H^i(\operatorname{coker}(u))\to H^{i+1}(K^\bullet)\to\cdots$ (snake lemma in the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O)$, Stacks Lemma 0117), so every $H^i(\pi)$ is an isomorphism. Thus $\pi$ is a quasi-isomorphism in the sense of [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. (Equivalently, [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] applied to $0\to A^\bullet\xrightarrow{u}A^\bullet\to\operatorname{coker}(u)\to0$ exhibits $\varinjlim_n E_n^\bullet$ as a cone of $Q(u)$ in $D(\Mod(\mathcal O))$; the explicit $\pi$ above is what makes the comparison map canonical.)
